CosmosAI learning illustrations
The original drawings are project-authored Excalidraw scenes. Web copies are exported with @excalidraw/utils 0.1.5, an MIT-licensed build-time dependency. The browser does not load the Excalidraw editor or its JavaScript bundle.
Exported SVGs include font subsets to render without remote font requests: - Virgil, created by Ellinor Rapp, SIL Open Font License 1.1. https://github.com/excalidraw/virgil/blob/main/LICENSE.md - Cascadia Code, Microsoft Corporation, SIL Open Font License 1.1. https://github.com/microsoft/cascadia-code/blob/main/LICENSE
License texts accompany this notice in Excalidraw-MIT.txt, Virgil-OFL.txt and Cascadia-Code-OFL.txt. The fonts' licenses apply to their embedded font data, not to the surrounding project-authored teaching content.

svg.title: Our tiny CNN: pixels, features, classes and changing weights

g.text: Our tiny CNN: pixels, features, classes and changing weights
Measured run: seed 7 | CPU float32 | 2 train images | batch 2 | 2 epochs | SGD learning rate 0.1
Concept: matrices, gradients and changing weights
1. Connections: internal features feed class scores, NOT other classes
Node numbers: first image BEFORE update 1. Connection colors: numerical weight movement DURING update 1.
Blue: weight moves UP. Orange: DOWN. Thickness: gradient magnitude, not a neuron importance score.
Convolution shares filter weights across pixels. Only this 4-to-4 classifier is drawn as all 16 individual connections.
2. Matrix multiplication: W @ a + b = logits
Rows of W are classes; columns are pooled features. This repeats one weighted sum for each class, not one image per row.
The final layer has no sigmoid. Softmax follows for displayed probabilities; cross entropy uses the raw logits.
PyTorch batches use rows: Z = A @ W.T + b. Two images -> A shape (2,4) -> Z shape (2,4). Same weighted sums.
Concept: the matrix and vector notation
3. Backward: fill gradient tensors, leave W unchanged
One scalar loss has a derivative for each of our 132 parameters. The videos sometimes show NEGATIVE gradient; these values are gradient.
One connection: W[1,1], feature 1 -> spiral score
For each W[i,j]: average (P(class i) - target) * feature j
One derivative per connection, NOT one global weight update.
Confirmed by snapshot: weights BEFORE backward == weights AFTER backward. Only .grad received the new derivatives.
Code: before_step() reads the actual .grad tensors
Concept: where these gradients come from
4. Optimizer: the same matrix changes twice
new_weight = old_weight - 0.1 * gradient. Each weight has its own gradient; biases and convolution filters update too.
Blue cells increased numerically; orange decreased. W1 becomes the next starting matrix: no reset between epochs.
For a fixed positive feature: support becomes suppression.
Still negative, but less suppressive. Not larger magnitude.
Code: after_step() snapshots actual changed parameters
Concept: SGD changes weights using gradients
5. Zoom BACK to earlier 3x3 filter weights, NOT the final output
features.0.weight[0,0,:,:]: output filter 0, red input channel. This is ONE of 12 RGB kernel slices, reused across image positions.
Top-left: +0.013442 -> +0.014060 -> +0.014711. Bottom-left: -0.112743 stays unchanged; both gradients are zero.
Center convolution: add all 27 matching pixel*weight products and ONE bias -> 0.037116. Open the full calculation.
ReLU keeps this positive center value. Averaging all 9 ReLU outputs gives a[0] = 0.020664 before training.
Concept: filters share weights across pixels
6. New features + new W + new b -> a new prediction
A read-only forward pass after each update checks the SAME batch. This does not run backward or another optimizer step.
Each update changed 116 weights + all 8 biases = 124/132 parameters. Eight convolution weights did not change.
Image B remains misclassified. Lower loss on two synthetic fixtures is not evidence of useful galaxy accuracy.
Full precision and all 264 scalar rows: docs/observations/galaxy_weight_updates_seed7.json and .csv. Display values are rounded.
7. Sigma / sigmoid vs ReLU: same input, different activation
First image, filter 0, BEFORE update 1. Our CNN uses ReLU. Sigmoid below is a separate calculation, not our training run.
max(0, z): zero negatives; keep positives
Concept: lowercase sigma vs uppercase SUM
Concept: sigmoid, used in the video
Average over 9 positions: actual ReLU -> a[0] = 0.020664; hypothetical sigmoid -> 0.485872. Different features feed later scores.
Center z = +0.037116: ReLU gives 0.037116; sigmoid gives 0.509278. Neither operation updates weights.
Backward, actual ReLU: incoming gradient 0.014745 passes at the positive center; the negative top-left position blocks it.
Concept: sigmoid is not four-class softmax
A sigmoid activation is not automatically a class probability. Our final Linear outputs logits; softmax is only for reported probabilities.
Concept: all calculations on our saved input
Read first: PIXELS -> FEATURE MAPS -> POOLED FEATURES -> CLASS SCORES
a[0] means feature zero, not phase zero or class zero. W is weights, not probabilities. The final output is FOUR numbers.
A. One input image, examined by four filters
Image A = gz2-000001: nine colored pixels, three RGB numbers per pixel. Not a real galaxy photo.
Center pixel (180,180,220) -> divide by 255 -> (0.705882,0.705882,0.862745). These are INPUT values.
The manifest labels this artificial fixture "spiral". That label is the target, not a property of the square colors.
Each filter uses three 3x3 weight slices: red + green + blue. 27 products plus ONE bias make each response.
Concept: what the colored squares mean
Concept: RGB kernel slices and center convolution
B. Four response maps AFTER ReLU -> average each map into one feature
Each map belongs to a different filter. Entries are computed responses at image positions, not RGB values or class probabilities.
Concept: pooling makes four internal signals, NOT four classes
C. Each class receives ALL FOUR features through its own row of weights
4 outputs x 4 features = 16 learned weights. Multiply each row by the four features above, then add that class bias.
Class 0 = elliptical by label mapping. It wins this INITIAL prediction, incorrectly: the target label for image A is spiral.
Concept: row i dot a + b[i] explained
Sections below zoom into these SAME operations and two weight updates. A later 3x3 kernel picture is not a later output layer.
Concept: full reading guide, including every number in the gradient example
0.294907 / 0.295825: predicted P(spiral) for images A / B.
1 / 0: target IS spiral / is NOT spiral (these are NOT class IDs).
/2: mean over two images. -0.061518: this weight's gradient.
Concept: what every number in this box means
Concept: why (probability - target) * feature gives this gradient
Concept: a kernel slice is learned weights for ONE color channel, not a prediction
